result:
I fixed 11 rules so they now behave the way their docstrings say. To check, I wrote a script that reads each docstring and the common rules in the module docstring, then compares every rule against that expected behavior over qty 0–299 and several unit prices. Before the fix, those 11 rules failed. After the fix, no rule fails.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | The cap was applied to the price, not the discount (`min(base, 30000) * 5%`) | Calculate the discount first, then cap it at 30,000 |
| 15 | A "whole" rule was using the "marginal" formula | Discount now applies to the full amount |
| 27 | Discount started at 101 units | Starts at 100 units |
| 40 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 | Always capped at 30,000 |
| 46 | Used 4% | Changed to 3% |
| 47 | Used `round` (rounds to nearest) | Changed to floor (`//`) |
| 55 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 200,000 | Always capped at 100,000 |
| 59 | Used 3% | Changed to 2% |
| 106 | `qty > 5` | `qty >= 5` |
| 107 | `qty > 50` | `qty >= 50` |
| 124 | A "whole" rule was using the "marginal" formula | Discount now applies to the full amount |

Rule 136 also used `qty > 5`. Its results were already correct, because a marginal discount is 0 at exactly 5 units, so I changed it to `>=` only to match the other rules.

The checking script is in `/tmp/chk/c.py`, outside the repo.

STATUS: DONE
